title: install_7z.py passes the NSIS /D= folder as a quoted argument, which fails for a Windows user folder with a space
goal: install_7z.install_exe runs the 7-Zip installer as one command-line string, the installer path quoted by subprocess.list2cmdline and then /S and /D=PATH unquoted and last (NSIS reads everything after /D= as the folder), without a shell, so a per-user folder that holds a space installs where it should

run:
import pathlib, sys, tempfile, types
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import install_7z as m
root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "Jan Kowalski" / "7-Zip"
root.mkdir(parents=True)
dest, seen = root / "7z.exe", []
def fake(cmd, **kw):
    seen.append((cmd, kw))
    dest.write_text("x")
    return types.SimpleNamespace(returncode=0)
m.subprocess.run = fake
try:
    m.install_exe(pathlib.Path("C:/Temp/7z-setup.exe"), dest)
    cmd, kw = seen[0]
    tail = "/D=" + str(root)
    ok = isinstance(cmd, str) and cmd.endswith(" " + tail) and '/D="' not in cmd and cmd.count("/D=") == 1 and " /S " in cmd and not kw.get("shell")
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e); ok = False
print(seen[0][0] if seen else None, ok)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Review G3 of SP-iir3d2tu (plausible, Windows only, not run): install_7z.py:156 runs subprocess.run([installer, '/S', '/D=' + dest.parent]); NSIS documents /D= as unquoted and last. Premise run on origin/main at planning (2026-11-10): the repro or first check fails there on the behaviour named in the goal; not fixed by an earlier commit.
